Formulae and molar masses from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; densities and colours are standard mineralogical values; molar heat capacities are Kopp's-rule estimates and explicit teaching approximations. No thermodynamic constant is asserted here: each phase is defined by the shipped database and matched to its species by composition — which is why langite is written here as the MONOhydrate Cu4SO4(OH)6.H2O. Mineralogical langite is the dihydrate; wateq4f defines the phase with one water, and the match is on exact composition INCLUDING waters of crystallisation, so a dihydrate entry would never have met the phase it was added for. The registry follows the database it has to match and records the discrepancy rather than hiding it

name: ammonium nitrate
provenance: ammonium nitrate: the cold-pack salt: dissolving it is strongly endothermic, which is the whole of an instant cold pack. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; density and appearance are standard reference values; the molar heat capacity is a Kopp's-rule estimate and an explicit teaching approximation. The enthalpy of dissolution, +25.7 kJ/mol, is the number the cold pack is for: one of the most strongly endothermic dissolutions a kitchen can produce, and the reason the pack goes cold rather than merely failing to warm.

electrical_resistivity.boundary: AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Graphite is strongly anisotropic - roughly 4e-7 ohm.m along the basal plane and some thousands of times more across it - and commercial grades differ widely. This value describes a polycrystalline bench rod or pencil lead, and is recorded so the meter can say 'a conductor, but a poor one beside a metal' rather than nothing. It supports no comparison finer than that.
electrical_resistivity.source: Kerotakis curated electrical-resistivity tranche v1: bulk DC electrical resistivity of the pure solid at 293.15 K (20 C), in ohm.m. THE PROVENANCE LANE OF THIS TRANCHE IS PENDING REVIEW AND THE VALUES ARE RECORDED AS COMMONLY TABULATED. The CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics table 'Electrical Resistivity of Pure Metals' is the intended primary reference and these numbers agree with it to the precision quoted, but this is NOT a transcription from a positively identified copy of any single edition and no edition-level provenance is claimed: every row is flagged for reviewer confirmation against a positively identified copy before any stronger claim is made, exactly as the phase-transition tranche is. The values themselves are physical constants of the pure elements rather than anyone's compilation, and they are quoted only to the three or four figures that a room-temperature handbook column carries; no temperature coefficient, no purity dependence and no cold-worked or alloyed value is claimed, and each row's own `notes` field states what it does not cover. Graphite is the one row that is an order of magnitude rather than a measurement, and its note says so: graphite is strongly anisotropic and its resistivity depends on the grade, so the value here describes a polycrystalline bench rod and nothing finer. Compiled 2026-09-05

name: graphite
provenance: graphite: the layered allotrope of carbon — soft, opaque, and the one in a pencil. Separate from the registry's charcoal carbon and from diamond because the point of comparing them is that one element gives three different solids. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; density and appearance are standard reference values; the molar heat capacity is a Kopp's-rule estimate and an explicit teaching approximation.

name: diamond
provenance: diamond: the tetrahedral allotrope: the same carbon atoms as graphite, 55% denser, and transparent instead of black. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; density and appearance are standard reference values; the molar heat capacity is a Kopp's-rule estimate and an explicit teaching approximation. The bench has no transparency for a solid, so diamond is described as white rather than clear — the one property a person would name first is the one this appearance model cannot express. That is stated here because a reader who sees 'white diamond' should know it is a limit of the description and not a claim about the stone.

name: methane
provenance: methane, the simplest alkane and the main component of natural gas. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(g) 35.7 J/(mol.K) at 298 K: standard reference values. The NASA CEA record this species matches by composition is what makes it burn; density is the bench's shared gas placeholder of 1.0 g/mL, the same figure O2, N2, H2 and CO2 carry: a gas is added by the mole and its volume comes from the vessel's headspace, so no run reads this number. Odour is not modelled: the smell of a gas leak is the added odorant, not the methane.

name: propane
provenance: propane, the bottled-gas alkane. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(g) 73.6 J/(mol.K) at 298 K: standard reference values. It is entered as the gas because that is the phase it burns in; the liquid under pressure inside the bottle is a state this bench does not hold, so nothing here describes a cylinder. density is the bench's shared gas placeholder of 1.0 g/mL, the same figure O2, N2, H2 and CO2 carry: a gas is added by the mole and its volume comes from the vessel's headspace, so no run reads this number.

name: butane
provenance: butane, the lighter-fuel alkane, as n-butane. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(g) 98.5 J/(mol.K) at 298 K for n-butane: standard reference values. Isobutane has the same formula and is a different substance with its own boiling point; this record is the straight chain and does not distinguish the two, so a composition match may reach either isomer's thermochemistry. density is the bench's shared gas placeholder of 1.0 g/mL, the same figure O2, N2, H2 and CO2 carry: a gas is added by the mole and its volume comes from the vessel's headspace, so no run reads this number.

name: helium
provenance: helium, the monatomic noble gas. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(g) 20.8 J/(mol.K) is 5R/2, exact for an ideal monatomic gas and the reason helium's heat capacity is the same at every temperature a bench reaches. Chemically it does nothing at all, which is the point of having it: whatever pressure it makes in a sealed vessel is the pressure the amount of substance makes, with no chemistry underneath. density is the bench's shared gas placeholder of 1.0 g/mL, the same figure O2, N2, H2 and CO2 carry: a gas is added by the mole and its volume comes from the vessel's headspace, so no run reads this number.

name: naphthalene
provenance: naphthalene, the fused two-ring aromatic sold as mothballs. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; density 1.14 g/mL and Cp(s) 165.7 J/(mol.K) at 298 K: standard reference values. The aqueous solubility of 0.003 g/100 mL is the reviewed room-temperature figure and is entered so the bench can say it does not dissolve rather than apologise for not knowing. Appearance is recorded as white; the smell, which is the property a person would name first, is not modelled at all.

transitions.boundary: naphthalene sublimes appreciably at room temperature - that is what makes a mothball shrink in a drawer - and this bench models neither that vapour pressure nor the loss of mass it causes. What is recorded here is the ordinary melting and boiling of the solid at one atmosphere, which is a different claim
transitions.source: Kerotakis curated phase-transition tranche v1: normal melting, boiling, sublimation, decomposition and hydrate-dehydration temperatures at 101.325 kPa. Each value is an individually entered editorial constant, taken from the standard published values for these substances and cross-checked against general reference tables. It is NOT a transcription from a positively identified copy of any single handbook edition, and no edition-level provenance is claimed: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 97th ed. is the intended primary reference and every value here is flagged for reviewer confirmation against a positively identified copy of it before any stronger claim is made. (Reviewer confirmation recorded 2026-09-01 in the registry source's own citation; this seed constant is historical - the bootstrap only fires when the source record is absent.) Values are recorded only to the precision a school apparatus resolves; where a substance decomposes or sublimes rather than melting, no melting point is claimed at all; and where two general references disagreed the value was dropped rather than averaged or guessed. Compiled 2026-08-29

name: hydrogen sulfide
provenance: hydrogen sulfide, the gas that tarnishes silver and that a rotten egg smells of. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(g) 34.2 J/(mol.K) at 298 K: standard reference values. It is recorded as colourless because it is; the smell is the property that matters most about it in a room and this bench has no odour entry for it, so nothing in a run will warn a reader by nose. No sulfide solution chemistry is installed either: there is no S(-2) species on the shelf, so this gas dissolves into nothing and forms no metal sulfide. density is the bench's shared gas placeholder of 1.0 g/mL, the same figure O2, N2, H2 and CO2 carry: a gas is added by the mole and its volume comes from the vessel's headspace, so no run reads this number.

name: chlorophyll a
provenance: chlorophyll a, the magnesium porphyrin that makes a leaf green. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights over the accepted C55H72MgN4O5 formula; density 1.079 g/mL is a standard reference value and the molar heat capacity is a Kopp's-rule estimate and an explicit teaching approximation. No InChIKey is asserted: this record stands for the chlorophyll of a leaf, and chlorophyll b and the several allomers a real extract contains are not distinguished. The colour is RECORDED, not computed: chlorophyll looks green because it absorbs strongly in the blue near 430 nm and in the red near 665 nm and reflects what is left, and this species carries no absorption spectrum, so nothing in a run derives the green from those two bands. Photosynthesis is not modelled anywhere on this bench, so holding the pigment is not holding the process.

name: nylon 6,6 (repeat unit)
provenance: nylon 6,6 as one adipamide repeat unit, the same polymer-as-population convention polyethylene and PET already use. Molar mass from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights over the repeat unit; density 1.14 g/mL is a standard reference value and the molar heat capacity is a Kopp's-rule estimate and an explicit teaching approximation. No InChIKey is asserted, because a chain of indefinite length is not a molecule. NO aqueous solubility is entered either, and that is deliberate: the other polymers on this shelf carry a reviewed zero so the bench can say they do not dissolve, but nylon IS attacked by hot concentrated acid - the amide bond hydrolyses - and no solver here models that. Entering a zero would turn a gap into the claim that the polymer survives, so this record stays silent and the engine says it does not know.

name: uranium
provenance: M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(s) and density are the standard reference room-temperature values for alpha-uranium. This entry exists so the bench can answer whether a block of uranium warms itself through its own decay (curiosity corpus th-122), and it is a metal on a ledger rather than a metal on a shelf: no acquisition, handling, storage or disposal claim is made or implied by its presence here. The block is modelled as pure U-238; natural uranium's specific activity is about twice this, because U-234 at roughly 54 ppm sits in secular equilibrium with U-238 and contributes almost as many decays again, and the 0.72% U-235 adds a little more. The L0 safety screen has no radiological class, so uranium is filed there by its chemistry alone - it is an active metal and displaces hydrogen from acid - which is wrong about the world in the same way the lead row already says it is, and is written down rather than hidden
